editorial:
You know those movies that throw you right into the chaos from the first few minutes? Into the Storm is exactly that. Set in the small town of Silverton, the story follows everyday people, storm chasers, and a high school vice principal as an ordinary day turns into a nightmare of tornadoes. The found-footage style puts you right in the middle of the action, making every flying car and collapsing building feel close and real. It is not deep or fancy, but it moves fast and keeps your heart racing.

The action scenes are the real star here, with impressive special effects that make the tornadoes look terrifying and huge. The acting is decent, though the characters are pretty simple and you will not remember them long after the credits roll. Some dialogue feels cheesy, and the shaky camera can get tiring. Still, if you want a fun, loud disaster movie for a weekend night, this delivers. Grab it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the massive wedge tornado tears through Silverton, destroying everything in its path. Pete, the storm chaser, dies while trying to capture footage as his tank vehicle is lifted and dropped. Donnie and Kaitlyn survive being trapped in a collapsed building, and Gary reunites with his sons. Allison finds her daughter safe. As the storms finally pass, the survivors gather and reflect on what they lost and gained. The movie closes with the storm chasers' footage being shared, showing the world the power of the tornadoes they chased.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves disaster movies and big action set pieces.
